Whether the own-term end (June 30, 1949) or the revocation date (EO 10011, October 22, 1948) is the first end is a lifecycle question.
notice: Producer research decision only. Independent review and owner adoption remain separate.
rationale: I read the complete held EO 9982 original (13 FR 4375): one paragraph extending and continuing in effect the provisions of EO 9870 of July 8, 1947 (Foreign Service allowances and allotments) 'to and including June 30, 1949', effective as of July 1, 1948. I read the held EO 10011 text (13 FR 6263): paragraph 3(b) says 'Executive Order No. 9870 of July 8, 1947, and Executive Order No. 9982 of July 29, 1948, are hereby revoked: Provided, that existing rules and regulations prescribed pursuant to such orders shall remain in effect until superseded as provided in paragraph 3(a)'. EO 9982 is therefore named and revoked in full; independently its own term ended June 30, 1949. The proviso preserves rules and regulations issued under those orders, not the order itself. No other ending instrument is held and no earlier end is indicated; the catalog line 'Amends: EO 9870' is a lead only and the 1989 snapshot adds nothing operative. Exact end date and survival of regulations remain lifecycle gaps. Provisional NO hypothesis.
